result.summary: The image shows a residential intersection with a marked continental crosswalk and sidewalks on both sides. While basic pedestrian infrastructure like curb ramps is present, the crossing lacks active traffic control or warning signage, and a large tree near the corner may limit visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: A large tree located near the corner of the intersection may block sightlines between pedestrians waiting to cross and approaching motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-right, near the corner of the intersection.

interventions.title: Daylighting and Sightline Improvement
interventions.description: Ensure vegetation is trimmed or managed near the intersection to maintain clear sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signage
interventions.description: Install pedestrian crossing warning signs to alert drivers to the presence of the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position before they enter the roadway.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a marked zebra crosswalk across a multi-lane arterial road with a central refuge island. However, the presence of a high-speed right-turn slip lane and the overall wide crossing distance create significant conflict points and exposure for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Right-turn slip lane
hazards.description: A dedicated right-turn lane allows vehicles to maintain higher speeds while turning, increasing conflict risk with pedestrians crossing.

hazards.name: Long crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of high-speed traffic, increasing exposure time.

interventions.title: Reconstruct Slip Lane
interventions.description: Modify the right-turn slip lane to a tighter radius or a 'smart channel' to slow turning vehicles and improve sight lines.

interventions.title: Install Pedestrian Signals
interventions.description: Add pedestrian-activated signals or RRFBs to increase driver awareness and compliance at the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Completion
interventions.description: Extend and connect sidewalks to provide a continuous, paved path for pedestrians approaching the crossing.

result.summary: The image shows a wide, multi-lane arterial intersection with a 40 mph speed limit, creating a high-exposure environment for pedestrians. While sidewalks and basic crosswalk markings are present, the long crossing distance and lack of a refuge island or visible pedestrian signals prioritize vehicle throughput over pedestrian safety.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway requires pedestrians to cross multiple lanes of traffic without a refuge island, increasing exposure time.

hazards.name: High Speed Limit
hazards.description: A speed limit of 40 mph is posted, which significantly increases the risk of severe injury in the event of a collision.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The existing crosswalk markings are faint, reducing their visibility to approaching motorists.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Replace faded parallel lines with continental-style markings to improve visibility.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane or unused road space to shorten the crossing distance and improve sight lines.
